question: Detect sponsored projects filed under the project's own name with the host's EIN (e.g. 'SOL VIDA' and 'HAPPENSTANCE THEATER' under Fractured Atlas 11-3451703; 'Future Chefs' under TSNE 04-2261109): flag lines whose filed name shares no non-generic token with the EIN's BMF or modal filed name, restricted to the 347 keyed host EINs, and hand-check a sample to estimate the recall of the FBO-name rule
conclusion_affected: Fiscal-sponsor share of the exception proxy; recall of the de facto host list
rationale: Only 20 of 337 directory EINs and 13 of 20 Q-B15 EINs appear in any FBO / c/o line; 82% of valid project-style lines come from ImpactAssets, so name connectors miss most sponsored-project grants. Name-EIN mismatch is a second, filer-independent signal

question: Assets Under Movement / Amalgamated Charitable Foundation (EIN 82-1517696, $58.0m of top-50 FY2023-24 lines): read its FY2023-24 Form 990 Schedule D Part I and Schedule I to split DAF / pooled-fund pass-through from fiscally sponsored projects, and decide whether it belongs on the DAF-to-DAF whitelist rather than in the fiscal-sponsor category
conclusion_affected: Half of the $114.6m de facto addition; DAF-to-DAF whitelist coverage
rationale: It is the largest of the 5 hosts both lists miss (6 distinct FBO projects at ImpactAssets) and NTEE T30; without it the addition is $56.6m (0.061% of proxy dollars)

question: Second-filer validation of the de facto hosts: for the 11 hosts with >=3 FBO projects, check whether non-ImpactAssets sponsors' lines to the same EINs name the same projects in BusinessNameLine2 or in the Schedule I purpose column (GrantOrContributionPurposeTxt), which the line cache does not keep; re-parse the 94 XML returns to add purpose text
conclusion_affected: Whether the de facto host set is an ImpactAssets naming artefact or market-wide
rationale: 10 of 11 de facto hosts are seen only through ImpactAssets lines; only Players Philanthropy Fund appears across 3 filers. Purpose text often carries 'for X project' and would remove the single-filer dependence

question: Host-side confirmation for the 14 two-project intermediary hosts not yet counted (Digital Harbor Foundation $27.1m, Sustainable Markets Foundation $12.3m, Sustainable Economies Law Center, Resist, Project South, Center for Economic Democracy, Runway Root, MICA Group, Common Future, Allied Media Projects, WESPAC, Movement Alliance Project, Centro por la Justicia, EIN 842045603): read each host's own site or Form 990 Part III for a fiscal-sponsorship programme
conclusion_affected: Fiscal-sponsor share at the >=2-project threshold (0.50% / 2.14% vs 0.47% / 2.06%)
rationale: Moving from >=3 to >=2 projects adds 14 hosts and $69.0m; the hand check shows 90% sponsorship precision in the intermediary class but the threshold itself is a judgement

question: Directory hosts with large top-50 receipts and no project-style line (Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors $245.9m, 50CAN $94.2m, Global Impact $51.5m, Myriad USA $46.5m, Edward Charles Foundation $23.5m): sample 10 Schedule I lines each and read the recipients' own grant lists or 990 Schedule I to estimate the share that is project pass-through versus own programmes
conclusion_affected: Upper-bound status of the directory-only fiscal-sponsor dollars ($531.4m counted in the headline)
rationale: 201 directory EINs receive $703.2m of top-50 lines but never appear in FBO / c/o lines; filer naming cannot confirm or refute them, so a host-side check is the only route
